routes.title: Manufacturing and reporting
routes.requirements: Windows 11 x64 and a current browser. Python 3.14.10 is included; no Python installation, pip, account, admin rights or PATH change is needed. Other platforms can use the separate source ZIP with Python 3.12/3.13.
routes.exercise: Extract All into a new local folder, then double-click Workfloor.cmd. It opens the local report in your browser. On a fresh database, keep From date 2026-10-01 and Before date 2026-10-08. Run the report and compare the correct aggregation with the deliberately wrong join. Save a snapshot, stop with Ctrl+C in the console, then launch again and reopen it.
routes.expected: 9 orders / 365 units / 4 delayed. The incorrect join counts 26 rows / 1,195 units. The saved snapshot retains its original report after restart.
routes.limits: Synthetic demonstration with invented manufacturing records. Default private data lives outside the app under the Windows local application-data folder, Outlands/Workfloor/data. Existing data is reopened and never reset automatically. Automated qualification covers an isolated bundled runtime and Chromium on hosted Windows, plus local CLI/recovery checks; a manual Python-free-PC/Explorer test remains unperformed. The outer package is not Authenticode-signed. No factory/employer connection.

next.label: SQL Report Workbench for Windows
next.exercise: Windows x64: Python is included. Extract All and double-click SQL Report Demo.cmd. Click Run saved query for alpha/beta 8/11, change the query bindings to {"minimum":4}, then run for 5/11. The tutorial seeds one invented dataset and one query only on a new separate workspace; later records persist. The original source CLI demo still demonstrates revisions and 9/12. State-only backups omit snapshots and exports; stop all processes and copy the entire workspace for complete recovery.

routes.title: Build a local website
routes.requirements: Node.js 24 with npm, Windows or Linux, and a modern browser. npm ci downloads locked dependencies; the native SQLite binding may require compiler/SDK prerequisites.
routes.exercise: Follow the quick start to set a private password and a new data directory outside the app. In the fictional Cedar Workshop site, change a headline and Save Draft. Check the public preview, Publish explicitly, then restart using the same data directory.
routes.expected: The draft stays private until Publish; the local public preview then shows the changed headline. Published content and any newer draft persist after restart; sign in again because sessions expire.
routes.limits: A single-user local editor. Publish updates its local preview; internet hosting is separate. Dependencies and the Node runtime are not bundled. Backup/restore requires a stopped app and new destination.

next.label: Verify a stopped-site backup and restore
next.exercise: Create and verify a stopped-site backup, restore into a new directory, and reopen both the published page and newer private draft. The guide gives the exact commands and refuses existing destinations.

routes.title: Inspect and validate code
routes.requirements: Windows 11 x64 and a modern browser. Python 3.14.10 is included; no Python installation, pip, account, admin rights or PATH change. The separate source ZIP uses Python 3.12/3.13 on Windows or Ubuntu.
routes.exercise: Extract All, double-click Developer Demo.cmd, then choose sample-project from Saved project. Validate revision 1, review its checked/unchecked files and approve that exact validation. Select src/sample.py, edit and save revision 2, then compare 1 with 2. Validate again to see a new pending artifact; select the approved revision-1 validation and export its original source. Stop the server before maintenance.
routes.expected: After the exercise: 5 files / 2 saved revisions / 4 passing format checks / 1 explicitly unchecked Markdown file. The new validation starts pending. The approved nine-member private export stays pinned to revision 1.
routes.limits: Supplied project code is not executed. Passing syntax does not prove behavior or publication clearance. Demo and blank workspaces are separate and persist outside the app. The state backup omits inbox/exported files; stop every process and copy the full workspace for complete recovery. Package 0.1.1-1 wraps unchanged source declaring 0.1.0. Manual Python-free-PC/Explorer acceptance remains unperformed; the outer package is unsigned.

next.label: Release and developer QA workshop
next.exercise: Use the release-qa family ZIP and Python 3.12/3.13. Run python -B workshops/run.py --family release-qa --workspace NEW_ABSOLUTE_SCRATCH_DIRECTORY with a new absolute path outside the package. Expect three checked examples and eight commands, including deliberate differences. This does not establish installation or deployment acceptance.
